title: This Little Snake Rolls Like a Wheel to Escape
summary:
Snakes have many ways to stay safe. Some bite, and some rattle their tails. But the dwarf reed snake from Southeast Asia has a surprising trick. When it is in danger, it rolls away like a wheel!

This snake is usually less than 12 inches long. When it rolls, it can move about one foot every second. That is about four times faster than when it slithers. It can even roll in a straight line while keeping its head steady.

Scientists at Toho University in Japan filmed the snakes with high-speed cameras. These cameras show fast moves in slow motion. The scientists found that the snake whips one side of its body forward, then the other side, again and again.

It is a little like twirling a rope while holding one end still. For this snake, the end that stays still is its head. That way, it can keep looking ahead while it zooms away.
why_it_matters: It shows that animals can surprise us, so it is fun to watch nature closely and ask how things work.
